rachel.backstory: Baton Rouge raised, one of a big family, Ole Miss undergrad and LSU Law — the same track as John, which tells you something about how this household ended up. A genuine college football fan in her own right, not a spouse-adjacent one, a distinction she has never once had to make because everybody in this family already knows it. She turned in the quietest board in the group and the most contrarian one — Notre Dame under, Utah under, Auburn under, and James Madison over as the only swing anybody has to look up. Same bayou, same house, same water line on the wall. She has watched it come up and watched it go back down, and she tells that story at parties without once dropping her voice.
rachel.running_gag: James Madison. The whole group had to look it up. She did not.
rachel.fatal_flaw: Three of her four picks need somebody to be bad. She spends the fall quietly hoping.
rachel.thesis: Quietest board. Most contrarian. Same bayou.

dossier.known_for: Turning in the quietest board and the most contrarian one.

running_gag.headline: Everybody Had To Look It Up

john.tagline: Ole Miss first, LSU second, and he’d like the record to reflect that.
john.backstory: McComb, Mississippi, and still the best football conversation in the family. He was a high school star in McComb before most of this roster’s parents were born, went to Ole Miss undergrad, then LSU Law, then spent years in the Attorney General’s office building arguments for a living. He is an Ole Miss man first and an LSU man immediately after, and he will explain the ordering with the patience of someone who has explained harder things to worse audiences. Every college football take Zach has ever had was pressure-tested against this man first. His board is the argument stated out loud — Ole Miss over, Mississippi State under, and a straight face while his own brother takes the other side of it. The house is on the bayou and the bayou has been in the house. He has rebuilt once already, and he will walk you through the whole thing the way he walks you through an argument — in order, start to finish, no flinching.
john.running_gag: Ole Miss first, LSU second. Nobody asks for the ordering. Everybody gets the ordering.
john.draft_tendency: Backed Ole Miss, faded Mississippi State, and can tell you why in order.
john.fatal_flaw: Has never conceded a point in his life. He only restates it more precisely.
john.thesis: Ole Miss first, LSU second, and he'd like the record to reflect that.

dossier.known_for: Pressure-testing every take in this family before it ever reached daylight.
dossier.status: Ole Miss first. LSU immediately after.

vic.backstory: John’s brother and Zach’s uncle. McComb-born, spent years in Diamondhead, and recently moved to Abita Springs, Louisiana — a decision he is delighted with. He is here because he likes being in it with everybody, which is a better reason than most people in this pool have. He is the only manager who took every pick to the over, which is either conviction or the refusal to overthink a $10 bet, and with Vic those have always been the same thing. He is also on the far side of Mississippi State from his own brother. He is a bayou man too, and he has had the water in the house and rebuilt after it — a thing he brings up as easily as the move to Abita Springs, and with about the same shrug.
vic.running_gag: Abita Springs. You will hear about Abita Springs.
vic.draft_tendency: Unbothered. Four overs, no hedge, moves on.
vic.fatal_flaw: Four overs and no hedge, so there is no version of a bad season where he is fine.
vic.thesis: Four overs, no hedge, moved to Abita Springs.

dossier.known_for: Taking every pick to the over and not overthinking it.

running_gag.label: Running gag
running_gag.headline: Have You Heard About Abita Springs

pull_quote.text: Four overs. No hedge. Moved on.

gayden.backstory: Seven years older than Zach and running at a completely different RPM. Medical device rep in Denver, played college soccer at Furman, picked up jiu-jitsu a couple of years ago and is already a blue belt, training with his son, because he does not have a casual setting. He is not a died-in-the-wool college football guy, and his board proves it: Michigan State, Baylor, UNLV and West Virginia — not one team anyone else in this family has ever watched on purpose. He is also the man who walked his little brother into a mustard display in a Baton Rouge grocery store, an act that created everything you are currently looking at. He will take a joke. He will also take your arm.
gayden.running_gag: Still insists Michael Bradley was good. Has been wrong about this for over a decade. Will not stop.
gayden.draft_tendency: Three overs on teams nobody expects anything from, and an under on Gunner.
gayden.thesis: No casual setting. Medical device rep. Blue belt. Mustard incident.

dossier.known_for: Walking his little brother into a mustard display. Also: Michael Bradley.

pull_quote.text: Michael Bradley was good. I will die on this hill.

devin.backstory: Auburn undergrad, dad played receiver at LSU, so he's an Auburn man with an LSU fallback and a lifelong inability to pick a side cleanly. The only boy with three sisters, outnumbered his entire life, now has three kids and outnumbered again. Originally Birmingham, now outside Tampa, sales rep for a company that builds power line trucks. The name comes from the day he looked at a ghost pepper and said 'I can eat that.' He could not eat that. He then looked at Auburn over six and a half and said the same thing. He is also the reigning World Cup champion, a title he holds legitimately, permanently, and — depending on which cousin you ask — through the exploitation of a scoring bug. He has never once acknowledged the asterisk.
devin.running_gag: The title, and the manner of its acquisition.
devin.draft_tendency: Confident. Trusts the pick, waits it out.
devin.fatal_flaw: Took his own school to the over. His aunt took the other side without blinking.
devin.thesis: Auburn man. WC champion. The asterisk is not acknowledged.

dossier.known_for: The title, and the manner of its acquisition.

pull_quote.text: I looked at the ghost pepper and said I can eat that.

holly.backstory: Cousin to Zach and Gayden, niece to John and Rachel, and functionally a sister — she lived with them for a year in high school. Baton Rouge raised, Tennessee educated, currently residing in Chelsea, Alabama, surrounded on all sides by Alabama and Auburn fans, a situation she describes with the weariness of a hostage. Her board is her stated system executed without a single deviation: Tennessee over, Georgia under, Clemson under. She had every opportunity to take an Alabama or Auburn under and did not, which is the most restraint anyone has ever seen from her on the subject.
holly.running_gag: Living in Alabama and refusing to convert.
holly.draft_tendency: Picks against the teams whose fans have annoyed her most. Historically not a bad system.
holly.thesis: Tennessee educated. Alabama surrounded. Not converting.

dossier.known_for: Living in Alabama and refusing to convert.

running_gag.headline: Rocky Top in Roll Tide Country

pull_quote.text: I had every opportunity to take an Alabama under. I did not.

zach.backstory: The one who started this, and — because he wrote the scoring engine — the one whose scoring is now a family legal matter. Wake Forest, Baton Rouge raised, LSU heart, and enough of a college football obsessive that this pool exists mainly so he has more games to care about. The name is not a bit; his own brother walked him into a mustard display as a kid and the yellow never really came off. He built the site, the pipeline and the projection model for a bet you could settle with a handshake, then drafted his own alma mater and his own team, both to the over, along with two more overs for good measure. Four picks, four overs, zero hedges, one engine that could have told him better.
zach.running_gag: Every scoring dispute goes to the man who wrote the scoring.
zach.draft_tendency: Overthinks it, then drafts with his heart anyway.
zach.fatal_flaw: Built a projection engine that keeps telling him he loses. Shipped it anyway.
zach.thesis: Built the whole thing. Drafted with his heart anyway.

dossier.known_for: Building elaborate infrastructure for trivial stakes.

pull_quote.text: Four picks, four overs, zero hedges, one engine that could have told him better.

gunner.backstory: Holly's son. Played college soccer at North Alabama, now a physical therapist in South Florida, likes fishing, doesn't especially follow college football, and is going to be a problem anyway — because last time out he had the World Cup pool won on merit and lost it to a scoring system his cousin wrote. Devin's final-match blowout swallowed a season of better picks. Ten dollars. He was a good sport about it, which is somehow worse. He is also the reason Zach spent a full offseason believing Italy had qualified for the World Cup; he supplied that information, watched it take hold, and never corrected it. He then turned in the cleanest board in the family — four conferences, Purdue over three and a half, and not one word of explanation.
gunner.running_gag: The asterisk. He didn't lose, he was scored out of it.
gunner.draft_tendency: Says nothing, walks out with the best board.
gunner.fatal_flaw: Will let you walk off the cliff rather than raise his voice.
gunner.thesis: Holly's son. Cleanest board. Scored out of a win.

dossier.known_for: Having the World Cup pool won on merit and losing it to a scoring system his cousin wrote.
